name: readlinkat
synopsis: ssize_t readlinkat(int dirfd, const char *restrict pathname, char *restrict buf, size_t bufsiz);
description: The readlinkat() system call reads the contents of a symbolic link into a buffer. It allows specifying a directory file descriptor for relative paths, which are resolved relative to that directory instead of the current working directory. It operates similarly to readlink() but with enhanced path resolution capabilities.

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor; if pathname is relative, it is resolved relative to this descriptor; use AT_FDCWD for current working directory.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Path to the symbolic link; can be relative or absolute.

parameters.name: buf
parameters.description: Buffer to store the contents of the symbolic link.

parameters.name: bufsiz
parameters.description: Size of the buffer; contents may be truncated if too small.

return_value.success: Returns the number of bytes placed in the buffer (may indicate truncation if equal to bufsiz)
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: Search permission is denied for a component of the path prefix.
pathname is relative but dirfd is neither AT_FDCWD nor a valid file descriptor.
buf extends outside the process’s allocated address space.
bufsiz is not positive, or the named file is not a symbolic link.
An I/O error occurred while reading from the filesystem.
Too many symbolic links were encountered in translating the pathname.
A pathname, or a component of a pathname, was too long.
The named file does not exist.
A component of the path prefix is not a directory, or (for readlinkat) pathname is relative and dirfd is not a directory.
